sections.text: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।
Fix thy mind on Me, devote thyself to Me, sacrifice for Me, surrender to Me, make Me the object of thy aspirations, and thou shalt assuredly become one with Me, Who am thine own Self.

So we are concluding chapter nine today. Chapter nine, Raja Vidya, Raja Guja yoga. Yoga of Royal knowledge and Royal Secret.
And obviously the question last time, what is this secret? Well, we have discussed many times, the secret is, where does my happiness lie? All my life I was seeking one thing and one thing alone. That is permanent happiness and permanent peace. I have tried everywhere, I have tried in getting knowledge, learning things in this world.
I have tried in accomplishing things, achieving things, acquiring things in my relationships. But in the end, every happiness came with associated unhappiness. As we have learned through our life, anything which has the capacity to give me happiness has an equal capacity to give me unhappiness.
In our relationships we know exactly: the closer you are, the more chances of getting hurt. Even though we know what we are looking for and look everywhere in our life, we cant find our happiness. So thats the secret.
And whatever makes me find that will be the knowledge which will be royal knowledge. So Brahmagnan is the secret. Unless you have the Brahmagnaan, you will never find this permanent happiness.
And Brahma Vidya is the Raja Vidya. And why it is called Rajavidya. Raja Vidya is something which is available to all.
The road which is available to everybody, Rajmarg, anybody can pass through that road, not restricted. It is the Raja Vidya because it is available to all. So the Brahma Vidya is the Rajavidya because this knowledge is available to all.
Brahma Ghana is the royal sacred. Because everyone has a birthright to know that knowledge. And still none of us is capable of finding it easily.
So Bhagavan said that that is the knowledge, that is the secret. Im going to tell you which is Pavitram Ida Muthamam. It is the highest purifier.
Once you wake up from your dream, the waking state is the highest purifier of your dream state. All your problems of the dream state go away. So we have started learning that Brahmagna is the one secret I need to unlock.
And the key is the Brahma Vidya. And therefore rest of the chapter is spent in describing what Brahman is, what is the nature of Brahman and what my relationship is with Him. So we have elaborately seen that there is nothing in this world which is other than Brahman.
In his manifest form he becomes this Prakriti, this manifestation. Anything which I see is nothing but the manifestation of the same reality. From science point of view, we have discussed the singularity at one time because of the Big Bang.
It is now a plurality and someday it will recede back into singularity again. So the same entity which is pervading everywhere is the basis of this reality as we know. And then what is my relationship? You see its a relationship less relation that all the qualities of Brahman are in me because I am his manifestation.
I am nothing but that this world is created by the Creator out of his own self. Because there is no other material was available to Him. Only available material to create this world was his own self.
Because if you think that there is other material available then he obviously is not complete God. So we have to come to the conclusion that his self and this universe and myself is one and the same. But I just cant recognize it.
That is the Avidy which we have to dispel. So this knowledge will dispel that Avidya Bhagavan said and therefore it is Rajavidy. So we have learned the nature of the Brahman that everything is because of Brahman.
Everything resides in Brahman but Brahman does not reside in it. In other words, my limitations are not in Brahman. My ignorance is not part of Brahman.
The Creator with his power of Maya he creates this universe through the Mayapati. He is the Lord of Maya, Lord of this illusion. But I am under the spell of Maya and therefore Im in a Maya Jal.
Im in the web of Maya. I cant see it clearly what my self is. He said the Vidya which will take me there would be the Raja Vidya, that which dispels my ignorance about my own self.
When I start seeing my relationship clearly with him then I will be Dharmaatma. Ill be a righteous soul. So Bhagavan has talked about the why people cant see it because of the Moga Asa Mogha actions.
Ill find my happiness here, Ill find my happiness there. And thats where we are confused. But the Mahatma, they single pointedly seek that happiness at the source of happiness which is the Brahman which is the Almighty Lord which is my own self.
So what is my relationship with Him? He is as close to me as my own self. But there is no special relationship he is with me. Because I am a Dharmatma and others are not good people.
He says I am same to Samoham Sarva Bhulteshu. My relationship to them is same as my relationship to you, him, her, my relationship to my children. If they have my four children, thats exactly same.
But one is closer to me than another, because he identifies with me more, he writes to me more, he calls me up more, he comes to see me more -- so I have more relationship with him. The one who never calls me, never writes me, never comes to Thanksgiving dinner -- I have less relationship with him. But my relationship with all of them is exactly the same.
Samoham Sarva Bhuteshu -- everything and every being is made up of me alone. Therefore relationship is exactly same. Just as my relationship with my left leg and right leg exactly same.
Even though I rely on my left leg more because right leg is broken. So Bhagavan says Samoham Sarva Bhuteshru and each one is the birthright to know this. But because we are deluded, therefore I dont recognize it.
Just because I think that I have not done something right in my past that does not stop me from realizing this truth. Durachara -- Su is a prefix meaning supreme. Su-Durachara means one who is the highest sinner.
Even he has the right to realize me. Bhajate Mam Ananya Bhak -- once he single-pointedly identifies with me. Sadhu Eva Sa Mantavyaha Samyak Vyavasito Hi Saha -- once he is rightfully resolved, once he has completely realized what is the right way of living, what is his swadharma, then he should be considered a Sadhu.
This is Krishnas missionary zeal to expand the tent to its infinity. Everybody is in it, nobody left out. So once that person is rightly resolved, we must consider him as a good person.
Forget about what his past is all about. And the next verse says why that is because Kshhipram Bhavati Dharmatma. Once you have a right resolve, you very soon will become what you resolved to become.
See, its all about your conviction about what is right and what is wrong. What is the right action? What is the wrong action? What is the right way of living and what is the wrong way of living. This is the right way to live.
You will become that in no time. Bhagawan saswat shantim ni gachati. And you will achieve that in eternal peace.
Peace which I had been seeking all my life and I have blamed everybody other than me. Children are not behaving to my expectations. Once you resolve rightfully where your Santi is, you will in no time achieve it.
Satsvatsanti m ni gachadhi. Such a person will achieve that eternal peace in no time. Kaunteya Pratijanihi Na Me Bhaktah Pranashyati.
It is obviously a little pat on Arjunas back. Because the Pandavas, at no time during their life, ever questioned their relationship with Krishna or their faith in Krishna. So in our case also, if I have complete faith in that Supreme Lord who is myself, then my peace lies there.
Then Bhagavan says Na Me Bhaktah Pranashyati -- one who identifies with me will never be destroyed. Never be destroyed in the sense that he will never lose his peace again. Once I have decided where my peace is and am rightfully pursuing it single-pointedly, Bhagavan said he will never go back to getting unhappy again.
The next verse has been difficult for people to translate and understand. Mam Hi Partha Vyapashritya Ye Api Syuhu Papayonayaha. Then he described: Striyo Vaishyah Tatha Shudrah Te Api Yanti Param Gatim.
They also achieve my being. They are the people who are born in Papayoni. Correct understanding can only be gained if we can define Papayoni correctly.
Thats where the problem is, right? Because he actually enumerated and gave examples of classes of people who are born in Papayoni. It is very loosely translated as sinful birth. Well, then you have to define sin. Sin we have defined as a negative impression on my mind which is damaging to my chances of getting peace.
When my mind is agitated, no matter how much of a Gnani I am, I will not have peace. We know that when the mind is agitated with any negative impression, there is no peace. Papa is that which robs away my peace.
So Papayoni is the environment which has the most chances of creating negative impressions on my mind. Environment is not something I control. So if I am placed in that environment, it is not my fault.
It is not something I have chosen; I happen to be in that environment. In modern day, we call it the disadvantaged class of people, or minority. In India, Jains have fought very hard to be classified as a minority, and they finally got the same status as Muslims and Christians who are considered minorities in India.
It is not that they are saying, We are bad, just consider us. No, they say, We are disadvantaged because we are not the majority. So Papayoni creates an environment which has more chances of putting negative impressions on my mind. Bhagavan said that people who do not have the privilege of being in the most pious and best environment -- and those people are Striya, Vaishya, Tatha Shudra -- in which society, in which time of history, do you think that women have had the same rights as men, including in 2016? We know they are always disadvantaged. It is not their fault.
It is the societys fault if the way it is designed does not give them equal opportunity. There is a movie coming up, the Birth of a Nation. Its about how and I have not seen anything.
I just saw a clip on one of those talk show. They said that in the slavery days a black child and white child will be playing together till the age of about 11. About 11 they will decide that only now the black child has reached highest of his or her development.
So he doesnt need to be sent to school or do anything about it. He can now start working. White child will continue in his development of learning and going to school.
So is that something you consider a Papa Yoni -- because the child is born in that yoni, or because the society is not giving him an opportunity? Bhagavan said: the society which has not given them the opportunity they deserve -- an opportunity rightfully theirs, which is their birthright -- we are not giving them that. Even though you are born in that class of people who are disadvantaged, you have equal right to achieve the highest potential. In those days, and even today, there are classes which are disadvantaged.
Striya, Vaishya, Tatha Shudra -- women, merchants, laborers -- by history, everybody can vouch for it that they never had equal rights.

The final verse of Chapter 9 distills the entire teaching into four instructions: Man-mana bhava - fix your mind on Me; mad-bhakto - be My devotee; mad-yaji - sacrifice to Me; mam namaskuru - bow to Me. These are not four separate practices but one integrated orientation: complete absorption in the Divine through thought, feeling, action, and humility. The promise follows: Mam evaishyasi - you shall come to Me alone.
Yuktvaivam atmanam mat-parayanah - having thus united the self, with Me as your supreme goal. The Sanskrit parayana means ultimate destination, final refuge. When the Divine becomes your parayana - not one goal among many but THE goal that contains all others - liberation is assured. This is not about abandoning worldly responsibilities but about recognizing what they ultimately serve. The executive working to support family, the artist creating beauty, the scientist seeking truth - all activities can have mat-parayanah (the Divine as supreme goal) as their hidden foundation.
This verse appears again at the end of Chapter 18, framing the entire Gitas teaching. Chapter 9 reveals the royal secret: you are not separate from the Divine you seek. The path is simply the progressive removal of the illusion that you ever were separate. This week, make this verse your constant companion. When the mind wanders, return: Man-mana bhava - let my mind rest in You. When devotion wavers, remember: mad-bhakto - I am Your devotee, whether I feel it or not. When action becomes self-serving, redirect: mad-yaji - this is my offering. When pride arises, bow: mam namaskuru - I am not the doer; You are the source and goal of all.
